description: Evidence that kaiban-distributed's distributed runtime — the gate, board/HITL, A2A and routing paths the article's architecture relies on — passes its own end-to-end suite against a REAL message broker, not a mock.
config: vitest.e2e.config.mts in the kaiban-distributed checkout; its globalSetup starts and stops a Docker Redis container for the run
broker: real Redis in Docker (BullMQ transport), started and stopped by the suite's own globalSetup
exclusions: the e2e config excludes the kafka, live and chaos suites; they were deliberately not run
whatThisShows: The shipped runtime's end-to-end paths work with a real broker: board and human-in-the-loop integration, agent-to-agent protocol, completion routing, distributed execution, event isolation, fan-out/fan-in, horizontal scaling over BullMQ, and the security/governance integration suite.
whatThisDoesNotShow: It does NOT run the Carbon-Verdict Governor inside that runtime (this package plugs the governor into the same ActionGate in-process — see fitness/ and simulation/), it is NOT a deployment, and it says nothing about carbon behaviour. A full Docker stack (Kafka + Zookeeper, board and agent services) was deliberately not run: no claim in the article depends on it. That is future work.
